newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Digital set for growth, CEO Palmer says.
newsitem.headline: Digital set for growth, CEO Palmer says.

text.p: Digital Equipment Corp is well-positioned for growth after four years of investment, chairman and chief executive officer Robert Palmer said on Saturday.
"Digital feels very well-positioned at this time," Palmer told reporters at the opening of a laboratory.
Despite management shake-ups, restructurings and layoffs, Digital, the fourth largest computer company in the United States, has lost billions of dollars over the past few years.
But the worst is over, Palmer said. "Most of Digital's restructuring is behind it, I'm happy to say. It's been a very difficult four years that we've been going through."
Digital had "made investments during the last four years for where we believe the market is going," he said.
He said the company was now well-placed in products in 64-bit computing, Windows NT, and the Internet, which should be key areas of growth in the information technology industry.

Responding to a suggestion that Digital has been a leader in products and technology but a laggard in getting its message across, Palmer said recent consolidation of public relations, marketing and sales under one executive should "enable us to have a more coherent message to the marketplace."
However, Digital does many things, making it less easy to have a simple message than for companies that are not so diversified, Palmer said.
He said the Asia-Pacific region accounts for about 19 percent of Digital's revenue, up from 14 percent in 1992.
